events.content:
Now I understand the shape of the problem. Currently `page.tsx` awaits one big fetch at the top before rendering anything — with `cacheComponents: true` (Next's PPR-successor flag), that means **nothing** can be prerendered into a static shell; the whole route is dynamic and gated behind the full-page `loading.tsx` spinner. I'll split the fetch into a per-request deduped cache, move data-reading into each leaf component, and give each its own `Suspense` boundary so the static shell (`

Dashboard

`) prerenders immediately while each section streams in independently.

events.content:
Clean now — `app/data.ts` is new (added file), and the four `app/*.tsx` diffs are the actual optimization. ## Summary The route was fully dynamic: `page.tsx` awaited one blocking fetch before rendering *anything*, so with `cacheComponents: true` no static shell could be produced — every visit hit the full-page `loading.tsx` spinner. Changes: - **`app/data.ts`** (new): wraps the dashboard fetch in React's `cache()` so all three sections dedupe to a single request per page render. - **`app/page.tsx`**: no longer async/awaiting data. The static `

Dashboard

` shell now renders synchronously; `CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, and `LatestInvoices` are each wrapped in their own `` with a lightweight skeleton fallback. - **`CardStats.tsx` / `RevenueChart.tsx` / `LatestInvoices.tsx`**: converted to async server components that pull their own slice from the shared cached fetch, instead of receiving props from the page. Verified with `next build`: the route now reports `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static shell prerendered at build time, dynamic sections streamed in independently per request — versus fully dynamic before.
